html:
The Ktunaxa, also called Kootenay or Kutenai, are an Indigenous people of the upper Kootenay and Columbia rivers, in southeast British Columbia, northern Idaho and northwest Montana. Ktunaxa ʔamakʔis means Ktunaxa land. Their language is an isolate, not related to any other.

They fished, hunted and gathered in the Rocky Mountain valleys, and paddled distinctive canoes with pointed ends below the waterline. Some bands crossed the Rockies each year to hunt bison on the plains, where they clashed with the Blackfoot. Their western neighbours were the Secwépemc.

The fur trader David Thompson built Kootenae House in their land in 1807. The border of 1846 split their territory between Canada and the United States. In Montana they share a reservation with Salish peoples as the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes.
